children: *Absence of a Fed Rate Hike on Wednesday Would Be a Big Surprise to Markets: Banque Cantonale du Valais
*Fed Is Unlikely to Raise Rates as Much as Market is Pricing in: Banque Cantonale du Valais
*Dollar Could Strengthen Over Short Term But Weaken Over Medium Term: Banque Cantonale du Valais
High Oil Prices Ensure Fed Will Hike Rates — Interview
By Jessica Fleetham

The recent sharp rise in oil prices is the key reason why the U.S. Federal Reserve is set to raise interest rates at its decision on Wednesday, according to the heads of asset management and investment strategy at Banque Cantonale du Valais.
A worsening conflict in the Middle East has pushed oil prices well above $100 a barrel, with Brent crude last trading at $105.56.

"The only reason that we can see for a hike would be the level of oil prices, which is extremely high," said Daniel Farquet, head of asset management and advisory. "So it would be preemptive of future inflation."
Current levels of core inflation have been fairly consistent and alone wouldn't necessarily justify a rate hike, he said.
U.S. money markets priced a 91% chance of a rate hike on Wednesday just ahead of the decision, which is due at 1800 GMT, LSEG data showed.
If the Fed were to hold rates this would therefore come as a big surprise to markets, they said.

"It would actually cause some issues regarding the credibility of the Fed," said Gero Jung, head of investment strategy. He pointed also to recent data showing a strong U.S. labor market, as well as annual inflation that has been above target for a long time.

However, Banque Cantonale du Valais believes that after Wednesday's expected hike, the Fed won't raise rates as much as markets are currently expecting. Money markets have recently priced in a risk of as many as four quarter-point rate hikes over the next year.
"It's just too early to forecast four hikes, given the state of inflation now," Farquet said.

With the Fed expected to raise rates, the dollar has scope to strengthen in the near term. Over the medium term it could weaken, however, given that interest-rate expectations are probably overdone, they said.

The main focus for markets on Wednesday will be on the Fed's accompanying commentary and particularly the dot plot forecasts for an indication of how much and how fast rates could rise from here. The dot plot gathers Fed officials' forecasts, though Chairman Kevin Warsh has refrained from adding his projections.

"The main point is whether this will be a dovish hike or a hawkish hike," Jung said. In other words, investors will be looking to see whether Wednesday's rate increase is a one-off or whether it marks the start of a cycle of rate hikes, he said.
"I think that's the main issue that markets or analysts will focus on," he added.
